html:
Bryggen is the old wharf of Bergen, where German merchants of the Hanseatic League kept one of their main foreign offices, the Kontor, from about 1360 to 1754.

Bergen was then the largest town in Norway. Fishermen from the north brought stockfish, dried cod, to Bergen, and the Hansa merchants shipped it to Lübeck and the rest of Europe, bringing back grain the Norwegians could not grow. Their monopoly gave them great power over Norwegian trade.

The merchants lived in long wooden buildings along the harbour, unmarried and under strict rules. Fires burned Bryggen many times, and it was rebuilt each time to the old plan. The surviving houses, mostly from after 1702, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
sum: Bryggen is the old wharf of Bergen, where German merchants of the Hanseatic League kept one of their main foreign offices, the Kontor, from about 1360 to 1754.
